ideas.pitch: A real-time voice-to-code compiler that translates spoken architectural commands into clean, boilerplate-free TypeScript functions within a 12-hour web IDE.
ideas.title: VoiceCode IDE Assistant
ideas.why_it_could_win: In a frantic 12-hour sprint, judges reward tools that save developers tangible time; a snappy, working voice-coding extension will immediately impress live demo audiences.

ideas.pitch: An instantaneous semantic diff tool that analyzes a candidate's resume against a live job description and auto-generates optimized bullet points in seconds.
ideas.title: ResumeDiff AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses an everyday universal pain point for developers and job hunters, ensuring immediate relatability and a high 'I would use this' factor among judges.

ideas.pitch: A lightning-fast, offline-first voice ordering kiosk for local street food vendors built with local audio models and lightweight local storage.
ideas.title: QuickKiosk POS
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on high-utility local economic impact, a theme that consistently scores well with panel judges looking for real-world commercial viability.

ideas.pitch: An automated git commit and release note generator that reads repository diffs and produces standardized, readable markdown updates without manual intervention.
ideas.title: CommitZen AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Extremely tight scope makes it fully buildable and polished within 12 hours, ensuring zero bugs during the live demonstration.

ideas.pitch: An automated lecture-to-flashcard generator that ingests recorded audio or rough notes and extracts high-yield spaced repetition quizzes instantly.
ideas.title: StudySprint Flash
ideas.why_it_could_win: Appeals directly to the student demographic of the hackathon, providing a hyper-practical utility tool that everyone in the room understands and appreciates.
